sections.title: Kind words from people I have worked with

paragraphs: I am a Full Stack Software Engineer delivering scalable enterprise solutions across fintech, banking and tax compliance for clients including USAA and Vertex Inc. I bring end-to-end SDLC expertise in Java, Spring Boot, Angular, microservices, AWS and Azure, combined with hands-on experience developing AI agents and integrating multiple LLMs.

I use Claude, Specification-Driven Development (SDD) and Research, Plan, and Implement (RPI) methodologies to accelerate delivery. I have contributed to DevOps, Center of Excellence (CoE) and Vertex Agent Platform (VAPOR) initiatives spanning engineering improvements, enterprise metrics and application delivery, with recognition for innovation, internal platform development and multiple hackathon wins.

bullets: Designed and developed AI-powered engineering agents, including PR Fix and Fail-to-Fix agents, integrating multiple LLMs to automate development workflows, code analysis and issue resolution; collaborated with the VAPOR (Vertex Agent Platform) team to build cluster-based AI agents for end users.

Built TechScout, an end-to-end application using React.js and Node.js, contributing to frontend development, backend services, API integration and delivery; also enhanced the Connected Tax Platform (CTP) with application features, chat-based interfaces and AI-agent capabilities.

Contributed to Center of Excellence (CoE) initiatives by developing reusable skills, commands and AI agents that standardized workflows and improved developer productivity; collaborated across AI engineering, DevOps, CoE and platform development teams on organization-wide solutions and engineering practices.

Contributed to the Vertex Unified Metrics Platform to support centralized, consistent engineering measurement, while supporting DevOps and deployment workflows, including n8n deployments and automation that streamlined delivery and operations.

Applied Specification-Driven Development (SDD) and Research, Plan, and Implement (RPI) methodologies with Claude to structure requirements, plan implementations and accelerate AI-assisted software delivery.

Developed an in-house quiz application as an alternative to third-party solutions, earning organizational recognition and prize money. Also achieved multiple hackathon wins through innovative application development and AI-driven solutions.

Developed and maintained enterprise engineering applications using Core Java, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Spring Data JPA, RESTful Web Services and microservices across banking, insurance and enterprise-security projects for USAA and Citi Bank.

Contributed to USAA's Classic to Talon Migration (C2T) by analyzing legacy integrations, designing as-is and to-be API flows and developing migration strategies; designed, documented and published REST APIs using OpenAPI and Swagger 2.0 to improve discoverability and developer onboarding.

Integrated downstream APIs for secure microservice communication, optimized SQL queries and database operations, and implemented unit tests using JUnit and Mockito, achieving 85%+ test coverage and helping reduce production defects.

Deployed and monitored applications on OpenShift, analyzed pod logs through the OpenShift Web UI, and used Kibana and Elasticsearch to investigate application behavior, traffic patterns, active server instances and production issues.

Contributed to Citi Bank's Service Account Migration (SAM) by migrating service accounts to CyberArk, implementing secure integrations with Core Java and Spring Boot, and decommissioning deprecated accounts to strengthen credential security and reduce attack surface.

work.title: PR Fix Agent
work.text: An automated code reviewer for pull requests. When a developer opens or updates a pull request, the agent reviews the changes, looks for bugs, security risks and quality problems, and posts clear feedback with suggested fixes and examples directly on the pull request. It works like a reviewer who is always available.
work.result: Developers get feedback on bugs and security issues before a human review starts.

work.title: Fail-to-Fix Agent
work.text: When an automated test run fails, this agent reads the test results, finds what failed and suggests fixes. It uses earlier fix attempts as context, so suggestions for similar failures can build on what worked before, and it posts them on the pull request as a clear review comment.
work.result: Gives developers a starting point for fixing failed tests right where they already work.

work.title: Vertex Agent Platform (VAPOR)
work.text: An internal platform where teams build, run and manage AI agents in one place. It provides the agent runtime, an approved catalog of models and tools, safety guardrails, a readiness check before release, and monitoring of every run. Teams bring their own use case and data, and the platform handles the rest.
work.role: Built AI agents together with the platform team
work.result: Teams can move from an idea to a working, governed agent without building all the infrastructure themselves.

work.title: TechScout
work.text: A self-service web application where employees request new technologies and follow the request until it is approved or rejected. Each request moves through clear steps such as submission, review, evaluation and decision, with the right people involved at each step. It replaces scattered ticket tracking with one simple, visible workflow. I worked on the frontend, backend services, API integration and delivery.
work.role: Full stack developer: frontend, backend services and delivery
work.result: Everyone can see where a request stands, and reviewers get one clear place to work.

work.title: Connected Tax Platform
work.text: A web platform that brings tax products together into one connected experience. Instead of moving between separate products, customers follow their everyday tax tasks from start to finish in one place, with a single entry page, clear navigation, dashboards, a chat assistant and AI-agent help. I added application features, chat-based interfaces and AI-agent capabilities.
work.role: Built features across the user interface and AI-agent integration
work.result: Customers get one clear place to work, with AI help next to their tasks.

work.title: Vertex Unified Metrics Platform
work.text: A shared way to measure how products and engineering are doing. Instead of every team counting things in its own way, the platform collects measurements such as product usage, delivery speed, testing status and service health in one place, using common definitions, and shows them in dashboards that leaders and teams can both read. I contributed to it, along with DevOps work and deployment automation.
work.role: Contributed to the platform, and to DevOps and deployment automation
work.result: Teams and leaders look at the same numbers, defined in the same way.

skillInfo.name: Java 8/11/17
skillInfo.what: Java is a widely used programming language for business software. Versions 8, 11 and 17 are long-term releases that companies stay on for years because they are stable and supported.
skillInfo.analogy: Think of the versions as editions of a trusted company handbook: the rules stay the same, but each edition adds clearer chapters and removes outdated pages.

skillInfo.name: Python
skillInfo.what: Python is a beginner-friendly language that reads almost like English. It is popular for automation, data work, scripting and AI.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a Swiss army knife on an office desk: not the fastest tool for every job, but handy for almost everything.

skillInfo.name: TypeScript
skillInfo.what: TypeScript is JavaScript with types added. You describe what kind of data each piece of code expects, and mistakes are caught before the app runs.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a form with labelled boxes. You cannot write a phone number in the date box, so errors are noticed early.

skillInfo.name: JavaScript
skillInfo.what: JavaScript is the language that makes web pages interactive. It runs in every browser, and also on servers.
skillInfo.analogy: If a web page is a building, HTML is the walls, CSS is the paint, and JavaScript is the electricity that makes lights, doors and lifts work.

skillInfo.name: Spring Boot
skillInfo.what: Spring Boot is a Java framework that sets up a ready-to-run application with sensible defaults, so developers write business logic instead of configuration.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like moving into a furnished office: desks, power and internet are already there, so you can start working on day one.

skillInfo.name: Spring Data JPA
skillInfo.what: Spring Data JPA lets a Java application save and read database records without writing most of the database code by hand.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a filing assistant. You say 'get me all invoices for this customer' and the assistant knows which cabinet to open.

skillInfo.name: Spring Cloud
skillInfo.what: Spring Cloud is a set of tools for building applications made of many small services, such as configuration, service lookup and routing.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like the facilities team for a large campus: it keeps the directory, the signage and the shared rules in one place so every building works together.

skillInfo.name: Hibernate
skillInfo.what: Hibernate is a Java library that maps objects in code to tables in a database, so developers work with objects instead of raw database commands.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a translator between two languages. You speak Java, the database speaks SQL, and Hibernate converts in both directions.

skillInfo.name: JAX-RS
skillInfo.what: JAX-RS is the standard Java way to build web services that other programs can call over the internet using simple web addresses.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a restaurant menu with numbered dishes. Any customer who knows the menu can place an order without talking to the chef.

skillInfo.name: Angular
skillInfo.what: Angular is a framework from Google for building large, well-organised web applications with reusable screen components.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like building with ready-made furniture modules: each part has a clear shape and place, so a big office layout stays tidy.

skillInfo.name: Node.js 18
skillInfo.what: Node.js lets JavaScript run on a server instead of only in a browser. Version 18 was a long-term release used for APIs and tools.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like teaching a front-desk receptionist to also run the back office, using the same language they already know.

skillInfo.name: Dependency Injection
skillInfo.what: Dependency injection means a piece of code is handed what it needs instead of creating it itself. This makes code easier to change and test.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a chef who is given ingredients by the kitchen team instead of shopping personally. Swap the ingredients and the recipe still works.
links: Inversion of Control and Dependency Injection (Martin Fowler) | https://martinfowler.com/articles/injection.html

skillInfo.name: AI Agent Development
skillInfo.what: An AI agent is software that uses a language model to pursue a goal. It plans steps, uses tools such as search or APIs, and checks its own results.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a capable assistant who does not only answer questions but books the meeting room, sends the invite and tells you when it is done.

skillInfo.name: LLM Integration
skillInfo.what: LLM integration means connecting a large language model to a real product, sending it the right information and using its answers safely.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like hiring an expert consultant by phone. You must brief them clearly, and you decide what to do with their advice.

skillInfo.name: GPT Models
skillInfo.what: GPT models are large language models from OpenAI that read and write text, code and more. They power many chat and automation tools.
skillInfo.analogy: They are like a very well-read colleague who has skimmed a huge library and can draft, summarise and explain quickly, though you still check the details.

skillInfo.name: Agentic Workflows
skillInfo.what: An agentic workflow splits a larger job into steps where an AI decides what to do next, calls tools and can review its own work.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a project manager who breaks a task into steps, assigns each one and checks the result before moving on.

skillInfo.name: AI-Powered Automation
skillInfo.what: AI-powered automation uses AI to handle routine work such as sorting requests, drafting replies or moving data between tools.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a mailroom that reads each letter, decides which desk it belongs to and delivers it, without someone sorting by hand.

skillInfo.name: Claude
skillInfo.what: Claude is an AI assistant made by Anthropic. It can write, analyse and reason about text and code, and can be connected to tools.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a patient senior colleague you can ask to read a long document or review code and explain what they found.

skillInfo.name: GitHub Copilot
skillInfo.what: GitHub Copilot is an AI pair programmer inside the code editor. It suggests code, explains code and can help review changes.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a second pair of hands at the keyboard that finishes your sentence, while you stay the author.
links: GitHub Copilot on the GitHub blog | https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/

skillInfo.name: Cursor
skillInfo.what: Cursor is a code editor built around AI. You can ask it to explain, change or write code across a whole project.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a word processor where you can say 'tidy up this whole report' and it edits many pages for you to approve.

skillInfo.name: Rovo
skillInfo.what: Rovo is Atlassian's AI assistant that searches and answers across tools like Jira and Confluence.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a company librarian who knows every shelf and can answer 'where did we decide this?' in seconds.

skillInfo.name: Specification-Driven Development (SDD)
skillInfo.what: In specification-driven development you write down clearly what should be built before any code, and use that written spec to guide people and AI.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like an architect's blueprint. Builders, inspectors and clients all work from the same drawing instead of guessing.

skillInfo.name: Research, Plan, Implement (RPI)
skillInfo.what: RPI is a working method with three steps: first study the existing code, then write a plan, and only then build, with a review at each step.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like planning a trip. You check the map, write the route, and only then start driving.

skillInfo.name: Prompt Engineering
skillInfo.what: Prompt engineering is the skill of writing clear instructions and examples for an AI so it gives useful, reliable answers.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like briefing a new team member. The clearer the brief, the better the first draft.

skillInfo.name: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
skillInfo.what: MCP is an open standard that lets AI assistants connect to tools and data sources in one consistent way.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a universal plug. Any device with the right plug works in any socket, so you do not need a new adapter for every pair.

skillInfo.name: AI Agent Governance
skillInfo.what: AI agent governance means setting rules, approvals, limits and monitoring so AI agents act safely and can be audited.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like staff policies and sign-off limits. A new employee can do a lot, but large payments still need a manager's approval.

skillInfo.name: Code Review Automation
skillInfo.what: Code review automation uses tools or AI to check code changes for bugs, security issues and style, before a human reviewer looks.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a spell-checker for code. It catches the obvious slips so the human editor can focus on the story.

skillInfo.name: CI/CD Failure Analysis
skillInfo.what: When an automated build or test fails, failure analysis finds why and what to fix. Doing it automatically saves developers from reading long logs.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a car's diagnostic port. Instead of listening for strange noises, you read the exact fault code.

skillInfo.name: Microservices
skillInfo.what: Microservices split one large application into many small services, each doing one job and able to be changed and released on its own.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a food court instead of one big restaurant. Each stall specialises, and one stall closing does not shut the whole place.

skillInfo.name: API Gateway
skillInfo.what: An API gateway is a single front door for many services. It routes requests, checks identity and applies limits.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like the reception desk of a large building. Visitors check in once and are sent to the right floor.

skillInfo.name: Service Discovery
skillInfo.what: Service discovery lets services find each other by name, even when their addresses change.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a company phone directory. You look up 'Payments team' and get the current number instead of memorising it.

skillInfo.name: Circuit Breaker (Resilience4j)
skillInfo.what: A circuit breaker stops calling a service that keeps failing, so the failure does not spread. Resilience4j is a Java library for it.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like the fuse in an electrical panel. When something overloads, it cuts the circuit so the rest of the house stays safe.

skillInfo.name: Event-Driven Architecture
skillInfo.what: In an event-driven design, parts of a system announce that something happened, and other parts react, instead of calling each other directly.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a notice board in an office. When a new order is pinned, whoever needs to react can pick it up on their own.

skillInfo.name: Distributed Systems
skillInfo.what: A distributed system is a group of computers that work together as one. It must cope with slow networks, failures and keeping data consistent.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a team working across several offices. They have to agree on facts even when phone lines drop.

skillInfo.name: Resiliency Patterns
skillInfo.what: Resiliency patterns are proven techniques such as retries, timeouts and fallbacks that keep a system working when parts fail.
skillInfo.analogy: They are like having a spare tyre, a backup generator and an alternate route. Trouble slows you down but does not stop you.
links: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter (AWS) | https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/

skillInfo.name: Design Patterns
skillInfo.what: Design patterns are named, reusable solutions to common software design problems, so teams share a vocabulary.
skillInfo.analogy: They are like standard floor plans for a kitchen. You adapt them, but you do not invent the layout from scratch each time.

skillInfo.name: Object-Oriented Design
skillInfo.what: Object-oriented design organises code into objects that hold their own data and behaviour, which models real-world things.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a company with departments. Each one owns its work and talks to others through clear requests.

skillInfo.name: SOLID Principles
skillInfo.what: SOLID is a set of five guidelines for writing code that is easy to understand, extend and test.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like good office organisation rules: one person per role, easy to add new roles and no hidden dependencies.

skillInfo.name: System Design
skillInfo.what: System design is planning how the parts of a large software system fit together so it is fast, reliable and can grow.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like city planning. You decide roads, power and water before the buildings go up, because changing them later is costly.

skillInfo.name: MySQL
skillInfo.what: MySQL is a popular open-source relational database that stores data in tables and answers questions written in SQL.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a very large, well-organised spreadsheet system where tables link to each other and can be searched in a moment.

skillInfo.name: PostgreSQL
skillInfo.what: PostgreSQL is a powerful open-source relational database known for reliability and rich features.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a well-run records office: strict about rules, very reliable, and able to handle complicated questions.

skillInfo.name: SQL Server
skillInfo.what: SQL Server is Microsoft's relational database, widely used in business systems and reporting.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like the finance department's trusted ledger system, built to work well with the other Microsoft tools around it.

skillInfo.name: DynamoDB
skillInfo.what: DynamoDB is Amazon's managed NoSQL database. It stores items by key and is designed to stay fast at very large scale.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a huge set of lockers where you find an item instantly by its number, without searching row by row.

skillInfo.name: SQL Query Optimization
skillInfo.what: SQL query optimization means changing queries and indexes so the database returns answers faster and uses fewer resources.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like adding an index to a thick book. Finding a topic takes seconds instead of reading every page.

skillInfo.name: Apache Kafka
skillInfo.what: Kafka is a platform that moves streams of events between systems reliably and in order, at high volume.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a conveyor belt in a sorting centre. Items keep arriving in order and each team picks up what it needs at its own pace.

skillInfo.name: Redis
skillInfo.what: Redis is an in-memory data store used as a very fast cache, session store and message broker.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like keeping the most used files on your desk instead of in the archive room. You get them instantly.

skillInfo.name: Valkey
skillInfo.what: Valkey is an open-source, Redis-compatible in-memory data store, supported by the Linux Foundation and major cloud providers.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like the same desk-drawer filing system, now run by a community so nobody owns the key.

skillInfo.name: AWS
skillInfo.what: Amazon Web Services is a cloud platform where you rent computing, storage and many other services instead of buying hardware.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like renting office space and utilities by the month instead of building your own building.

skillInfo.name: EC2
skillInfo.what: EC2 provides virtual servers in the cloud that you can start, size and stop on demand.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like renting a computer by the hour. You pick the size, use it and hand it back.

skillInfo.name: ECS
skillInfo.what: ECS is AWS's service for running and managing containers, which are packaged applications.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a shipping port manager that decides which container goes on which dock and replaces any that break.

skillInfo.name: Lambda
skillInfo.what: AWS Lambda runs small pieces of code only when something triggers them, without you managing servers.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a taxi instead of owning a car. You pay only for the ride, and there is no parking to think about.

skillInfo.name: Fargate
skillInfo.what: Fargate runs containers on AWS without you managing the servers underneath.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a serviced office. You bring your team and work, and the building provider handles the rest.

skillInfo.name: S3
skillInfo.what: Amazon S3 is cloud storage for files of any size, with very high durability.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a huge, secure warehouse with labelled boxes. You can store anything and fetch it by its label.

skillInfo.name: RDS
skillInfo.what: Amazon RDS runs relational databases in the cloud and handles backups, patching and failover for you.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like having a database caretaker who does the maintenance and nightly backups so you can just use the data.

skillInfo.name: IAM
skillInfo.what: AWS IAM controls who can do what in your cloud account, using users, roles and permissions.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like badge access in an office. Each person's badge opens only the doors they need.

skillInfo.name: CloudWatch
skillInfo.what: CloudWatch collects logs and metrics from AWS resources and can raise alarms when something looks wrong.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like the dashboard and warning lights in a car. You see speed and fuel, and a light comes on when something needs attention.

skillInfo.name: SQS
skillInfo.what: Amazon SQS is a message queue. One part of a system drops messages in, and another picks them up when ready.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like an inbox tray. The sender leaves a note and the receiver handles it when they have time.

skillInfo.name: SNS
skillInfo.what: Amazon SNS sends one message to many subscribers at once, such as emails, queues or other services.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a company-wide announcement. One message reaches everyone who signed up for that channel.

skillInfo.name: Microsoft Azure
skillInfo.what: Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform for hosting applications, storing data and running AI services.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like renting managed office space from a provider that is already connected to the tools your company uses.

skillInfo.name: Docker
skillInfo.what: Docker packages an application with everything it needs into a container, so it runs the same on any machine.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a lunchbox. Everything for the meal is packed inside, and it works the same wherever you open it.

skillInfo.name: OpenShift
skillInfo.what: OpenShift is Red Hat's platform for running and managing containerised applications at company scale, built on Kubernetes.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a managed business park. Many tenants share the site with security, utilities and rules provided.

skillInfo.name: Git
skillInfo.what: Git tracks every change to files, so many people can work on the same project and go back to any earlier version.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like Track Changes for a whole project, with a full history and the ability to merge everyone's edits.

skillInfo.name: GitHub Actions
skillInfo.what: GitHub Actions runs automated steps, such as build, test and deploy, whenever code changes.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like an assembly line that starts by itself each time a new part arrives, and flags any defect.

skillInfo.name: GitLab
skillInfo.what: GitLab is a platform for storing code, reviewing changes and running automated pipelines in one place.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a single workshop that has the storage room, the review desk and the assembly line under one roof.

skillInfo.name: Maven
skillInfo.what: Maven is a Java build tool. It downloads libraries, compiles code, runs tests and packages the result from one project file.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a recipe card that lists the ingredients to fetch and the steps to cook, so anyone can make the same dish.

skillInfo.name: Gradle
skillInfo.what: Gradle is a flexible build tool for Java and other languages. It builds, tests and packages projects quickly.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a more customisable recipe system that remembers what it already cooked and skips repeated steps.

skillInfo.name: Elasticsearch
skillInfo.what: Elasticsearch is a search and analytics engine. It stores large amounts of text and logs and finds results in moments.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like the index at the back of a very big book. You jump straight to the pages you need.

skillInfo.name: Kibana
skillInfo.what: Kibana is the window onto Elasticsearch. It lets you search logs and build charts and dashboards.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a control-room screen that turns piles of log lines into charts you can read at a glance.

skillInfo.name: RESTful APIs
skillInfo.what: A REST API lets programs talk over the web using simple, predictable addresses and actions like get, create, update and delete.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a library desk with clear request forms. You ask for a book by its code, and always get a standard response.

skillInfo.name: API Documentation
skillInfo.what: API documentation explains how to use an API: what you can ask, what to send and what you get back.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like the instruction manual for a device. Without it, people have to guess which button does what.

skillInfo.name: API Security
skillInfo.what: API security protects the doors that programs use to reach your data, using identity checks, limits and input validation.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like checking ID at the door, limiting visitors per hour and never letting strangers into the back office.

skillInfo.name: JWT
skillInfo.what: A JSON Web Token is a small signed note that proves who you are, so a service can trust a request without asking again.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a wristband at an event. Once you have been checked at the gate, staff just look at the band.

skillInfo.name: OpenAPI
skillInfo.what: OpenAPI is a standard file format for describing an API so people and tools can understand and use it automatically.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a floor plan that everyone can read. Tools can generate docs and test clients from it.

skillInfo.name: Swagger
skillInfo.what: Swagger is a set of tools built on OpenAPI that turn an API description into interactive documentation you can try in the browser.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a demo showroom. Visitors can read about a product and try it right there.

skillInfo.name: JUnit
skillInfo.what: JUnit is the standard framework for writing automated tests for Java code.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a checklist the code must pass every time it changes, run automatically in seconds.

skillInfo.name: Mockito
skillInfo.what: Mockito creates stand-in objects for tests, so you can test one piece of code without the real database or services.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like using a crash-test dummy. You test the car's response without risking a real person.

skillInfo.name: Postman
skillInfo.what: Postman is a tool for trying out and testing APIs by sending requests and viewing responses.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a test call centre. You dial the service and see exactly what it answers.

skillInfo.name: Playwright
skillInfo.what: Playwright automates real browsers to test web applications, clicking and typing like a user.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a tireless tester who opens the site every night and checks that every button still works.

skillInfo.name: Unit Testing
skillInfo.what: Unit tests check small pieces of code on their own, quickly, so mistakes are found as soon as they appear.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like testing each ingredient before cooking. A problem is easy to spot when you check one thing at a time.

skillInfo.name: Integration Testing
skillInfo.what: Integration tests check that several parts work together, such as the app and its database.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a rehearsal with the whole band. Each musician may be fine alone, but you check they play together.

skillInfo.name: Test Automation
skillInfo.what: Test automation runs checks by machine on every change, so quality does not depend on remembering to test by hand.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a security camera that watches all the time, instead of a guard who only walks past now and then.

skillInfo.name: Multithreading
skillInfo.what: Multithreading lets a program do several things at once, such as handling many users, while taking care they do not interfere.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like several cashiers serving a queue. It is faster, but they must not take the same item from the same shelf at once.

skillInfo.name: Connection Pooling (HikariCP)
skillInfo.what: A connection pool keeps a set of database connections ready for reuse, which is much faster than opening a new one each time. HikariCP is a popular Java pool.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like a pool of company cars. Staff borrow one and return it, instead of buying a new car for every trip.

skillInfo.name: Idempotent Processing
skillInfo.what: An idempotent operation gives the same result no matter how many times you repeat it, so retries never create duplicates.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like pressing the lift button twice. The lift still comes once.
links: Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency (Stripe) | https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency
Making retries safe with idempotent APIs (AWS) | https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/

skillInfo.name: Code Reviews
skillInfo.what: In a code review a teammate reads your change before it is merged, to catch problems and share knowledge.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like an editor reading a draft before publishing. A fresh pair of eyes finds what the author misses.
links: Best practices for peer code review | https://smartbear.com/learn/code-review/best-practices-for-peer-code-review/

skillInfo.name: Agile/Scrum
skillInfo.what: Agile is a way of working in short cycles with frequent feedback. Scrum is a common framework, with sprints and regular reviews.
skillInfo.analogy: It is like cooking and tasting as you go instead of serving the whole menu at the end.
